title: Rosa Bonheur's birth chart
metaDescription: Rosa Bonheur's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 25.4° Pisces. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Four of the nine placements whose signs are settled stand in Pisces — the Sun, Mercury, Venus and Pluto. The placements whose signs could change with an unknown hour are not counted. A cluster that size becomes the section the rest of the chart plays around.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: Measured rather than labelled, the Sun holds 25.4° Pisces: the third decan, whose classical sub-ruler is Mars. A water sign, read here in its third face.

blocks.title: Closer to the ground
blocks.text: Closer in, Mercury stands at 10.2° Pisces; Venus stands at 15.1° Pisces; Mars stands at 21.8° Leo. The tradition reads a mind that absorbs before it argues from Mercury, taste tuned to mood and undertow from Venus, drive that ignites on contact from Mars.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Nothing in the geometry sits closer than Uranus and Neptune: 2.0° from an exact conjunction. A conjunction is the least negotiable aspect in the scheme — no distance to argue across, so the pair arrives as a single instinct. Behind it, Mercury sextile Uranus at 3.1°, and Jupiter trine Neptune at 3.2° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. Each angle here was measured at every hour of the civil day and held; whatever the missing clock said, this geometry was in it.

blocks.title: The standing structure
blocks.text: The day-stable angles form no closed figure. Nothing funnels; each aspect is its own negotiation, which the tradition reads as a chart of separate treaties rather than one campaign.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The classical table has three entries for this chart. Mercury in Pisces at 10.2° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given; Venus in Pisces at 15.1° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Saturn in Aries at 25.5° is in fall. The old table grades terrain, not talent — a placement in fall works uphill, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Of the 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: 4 in water, 3 in earth, 2 in fire by element, 4 mutable, 3 cardinal, 2 fixed by modality. A water emphasis reads as porousness: the room is registered whole, long before it is analysed in parts. No settled placement falls in air — an absence the tradition treats as information, not as a defect. Mercury, Venus and Mars were retrograde — the backward drift a body appears to make as the Earth overtakes it, read in the scheme as a function that reviews before it releases.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Sagittarius into Capricorn during that day at the birthplace, travelling 12.2° between one midnight and the next. A birth time would settle it in a second; there isn’t one. So the Moon stays unnamed here — the alternative is a guess wearing the clothes of a fact.
